headers.//: vite-plugin-pwa emits sw.js. This rule said service-worker.js, a file that has never been built, so it matched nothing and the real service worker shipped with Hosting's default max-age=3600. A browser honours the HTTP cache for a service worker script whenever max-age is under a day, so for an hour after any deploy the phone re-read the old sw.js, saw no change, and kept serving the previous bundle from precache. The laptop picked fixes up and the installed PWA did not.
The registration script points at the service worker; a stale copy is the same stall one step earlier.
Names the bundles to load. Every asset it references is content-hashed, so caching the shell is what pins an old app.
Hashed filenames — a change is a new URL, so these can be held forever.
